import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import rateLimit from 'express-rate-limit';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
import { redis } from './services/redis.js';
import authRoutes from './routes/auth.js';
import productRoutes from './routes/products.js';
import cartRoutes from './routes/cart.js';
import orderRoutes from './routes/orders.js';
import dashboardRoutes from './routes/dashboard.js';
import webhookRoutes from './routes/webhook.js';

export const prisma = new PrismaClient();
export { redis };

const app = express();
const port = process.env.PORT || 5000;

// Middleware
app.use(cors());
app.use(express.json());

const limiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 1 * 60 * 1000,
  max: 100,
  message: { error: 'Too many requests, please try again later.' },
});
app.use('/api', limiter);

// Routes
app.use('/api/auth', authRoutes);
app.use('/api/products', productRoutes);
app.use('/api/cart', cartRoutes);
app.use('/api/orders', orderRoutes);
app.use('/api/dashboard', dashboardRoutes);
app.use('/webhook', webhookRoutes);

app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.status(200).json({ status: 'ok' }));

app.listen(port, () => {
  console.log(`🚀 Backend running on http://localhost:${port}`);
});
backend/src/routes/auth.ts
typescript
import express from 'express';
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
import { prisma } from '../server.js';
import Joi from 'joi';

const router = express.Router();

const registerSchema = Joi.object({
  email: Joi.string().email().required(),
  password: Joi.string().min(6).required(),
  name: Joi.string().optional(),
  role: Joi.string().valid('CONSUMER', 'FARMER', 'FPO', 'RWA', 'HORECA').default('CONSUMER'),
});

router.post('/register', async (req, res) => {
  const { error, value } = registerSchema.validate(req.body);
  if (error) return res.status(400).json({ error: error.details[0].message });

  const { email, password, name, role } = value;
  const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
  if (existing) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Email already registered.' });

  const hashed = await bcrypt.hash(password, 10);
  const user = await prisma.user.create({
    data: { email, passwordHash: hashed, name, role },
  });

  const token = jwt.sign({ userId: user.id, role: user.role }, process.env.JWT_SECRET!, { expiresIn: '7d' });
  res.status(201).json({ token, user: { id: user.id, email, name, role } });
});

router.post('/login', async (req, res) => {
  const { email, password } = req.body;
  if (!email || !password) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Email and password required.' });
  }

  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
  if (!user) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid credentials.' });

  const valid = await bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash);
  if (!valid) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid credentials.' });

  const token = jwt.sign({ userId: user.id, role: user.role }, process.env.JWT_SECRET!, { expiresIn: '7d' });
  res.json({ token, user: { id: user.id, email: user.email, name: user.name, role: user.role } });
});

router.get('/me', async (req, res) => {
  const authHeader = req.headers.authorization;
  if (!authHeader) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Unauthorized' });

  const token = authHeader.split(' ')[1];
  try {
    const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET!) as { userId: number };
    const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
      where: { id: decoded.userId },
      include: { farmer: true, fpo: true },
    });
    if (!user) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'User not found' });
    res.json(user);
  } catch (e) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });
  }
});

export default router;

typescript
import express from 'express';
import { prisma } from '../server.js';
import { cacheMiddleware } from '../middleware/cache.js';

const router = express.Router();

// GET /api/products?category=honey&search=kiwi&page=1&limit=20
router.get('/', cacheMiddleware(300), async (req, res) => {
  const { category, search, page = '1', limit = '20' } = req.query;
  const skip = (parseInt(page as string) - 1) * parseInt(limit as string);
  const take = parseInt(limit as string);

  const where: any = {};
  if (category && category !== 'all') where.category = category;
  if (search) {
    where.OR = [
      { name: { contains: search as string, mode: 'insensitive' } },
      { variety: { contains: search as string, mode: 'insensitive' } },
    ];
  }

  const [products, total] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.product.findMany({
      where,
      skip,
      take,
      orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
      include: { farmer: true, fpo: true },
    }),
    prisma.product.count({ where }),
  ]);

  res.json({ products, total, page: parseInt(page as string), limit: take });
});

// GET /api/products/:id
router.get('/:id', cacheMiddleware(600), async (req, res) => {
  const id = parseInt(req.params.id);
  if (isNaN(id)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Invalid product ID' });

  const product = await prisma.product.findUnique({
    where: { id },
    include: { inventory: true },
  });
  if (!product) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Product not found' });

  res.json(product);
});

// POST /api/products (admin only) – skipped for brevity

export default router;
backend/src/routes/cart.ts
typescript
import express from 'express';
import { redis } from '../services/redis.js';
import { authenticate } from '../middleware/auth.js';
import { prisma } from '../server.js';

const router = express.Router();

// Helper to get cart key
const getCartKey = (userId: number) => `cart:${userId}`;

// GET /api/cart
router.get('/', authenticate, async (req, res) => {
  const key = getCartKey(req.userId!);
  const cartData = await redis.get(key);
  if (!cartData) {
    // Fetch from DB if not in Redis
    const cart = await prisma.cart.findUnique({
      where: { userId: req.userId },
    });
    if (!cart) return res.json({ items: [] });
    const items = cart.items as any[];
    await redis.setex(key, 3600, JSON.stringify(items));
    return res.json({ items });
  }
  res.json({ items: JSON.parse(cartData) });
});

// POST /api/cart (add/update item)
router.post('/', authenticate, async (req, res) => {
  const { productId, qty } = req.body;
  if (!productId || !qty || qty < 1) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'ProductId and positive quantity required' });
  }

  const key = getCartKey(req.userId!);
  let items: any[] = [];
  const cached = await redis.get(key);
  if (cached) items = JSON.parse(cached);

  const existing = items.find(i => i.productId === productId);
  if (existing) existing.qty = qty;
  else items.push({ productId, qty });

  await redis.setex(key, 3600, JSON.stringify(items));

  // Upsert in DB as well
  await prisma.cart.upsert({
    where: { userId: req.userId! },
    update: { items },
    create: { userId: req.userId!, items },
  });

  res.json({ items });
});

// DELETE /api/cart/:productId
router.delete('/:productId', authenticate, async (req, res) => {
  const productId = parseInt(req.params.productId);
  const key = getCartKey(req.userId!);
  let items: any[] = JSON.parse((await redis.get(key)) || '[]');
  items = items.filter(i => i.productId !== productId);
  await redis.setex(key, 3600, JSON.stringify(items));
  await prisma.cart.upsert({
    where: { userId: req.userId! },
    update: { items },
    create: { userId: req.userId!, items },
  });
  res.json({ items });
});

export default router;
backend/src/middleware/auth.ts
typescript
import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express';
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';

export interface AuthRequest extends Request {
  userId?: number;
  userRole?: string;
}

export const authenticate = (req: AuthRequest, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
  const authHeader = req.headers.authorization;
  if (!authHeader) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Unauthorized' });

  const token = authHeader.split(' ')[1];
  try {
    const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET!) as { userId: number; role: string };
    req.userId = decoded.userId;
    req.userRole = decoded.role;
    next();
  } catch (e) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });
  }
};

'use client';

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ReactQueryDevtools } from '@tanstack/react-query-devtools';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [queryClient] = useState(
    () =>
      new QueryClient({
        defaultOptions: {
          queries: {
            staleTime: 60 * 1000,
            refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
          },
        },
      })
  );

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      {children}
      <ReactQueryDevtools initialIsOpen={false} />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

'use client';

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { getProducts } from '@/lib/api';
import ProductGrid from '@/components/products/ProductGrid';
import Hero from '@/components/layout/Hero';

export default function Home() {
  const { data, isLoading } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['products', 'home'],
    queryFn: () => getProducts({ limit: 12 }),
  });

  return (
    <>
      <Hero />
      <section className="max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 py-12">
        <h2 className="text-3xl font-serif font-bold text-ink mb-6">Shop the mountain</h2>
        {isLoading ? (
          <div className="text-center py-20">Loading...</div>
        ) : (
          <ProductGrid products={data?.products || []} />
        )}
      </section>
    </>
  );
}

yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: neharvest
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redisdata:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      PORT: 5000
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@postgres:5432/neharvest
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
      JWT_SECRET: dev_secret
      USDA_API_KEY: ${USDA_API_KEY}
    ports:
      - "5000:5000"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/app
      - /app/node_modules

  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    depends_on:
      - backend
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - /app/node_modules
      - /app/.next

volumes:
  pgdata:
  redisdata:

🟢 PHASE 3: WhatsApp Business API Integration
3.1 WhatsApp Service — backend/src/services/whatsapp.ts
typescript
import axios from 'axios';
import { redis } from './redis.js';
import { prisma } from '../server.js';

const WHATSAPP_API_URL = 'https://graph.facebook.com/v18.0';
const PHONE_NUMBER_ID = process.env.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID!;
const ACCESS_TOKEN = process.env.WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN!;
const VERIFY_TOKEN = process.env.WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN!;

export interface WhatsAppMessage {
  from: string;
  text?: { body: string };
  type: string;
  timestamp: string;
}

class WhatsAppClient {
  private phoneNumberId: string;
  private accessToken: string;

  constructor() {
    this.phoneNumberId = PHONE_NUMBER_ID;
    this.accessToken = ACCESS_TOKEN;
  }

  // ─── Send Text Message ──────────────────────────────────────
  async sendText(to: string, text: string): Promise<any> {
    try {
      const response = await axios.post(
        `${WHATSAPP_API_URL}/${this.phoneNumberId}/messages`,
        {
          messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
          recipient_type: 'individual',
          to,
          type: 'text',
          text: { body: text },
        },
        {
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${this.accessToken}`,
            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          },
        }
      );
      return response.data;
    } catch (error: any) {
      console.error('WhatsApp send error:', error.response?.data || error.message);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  // ─── Send Template Message ──────────────────────────────────
  async sendTemplate(
    to: string,
    templateName: string,
    language: string = 'en',
    components: any[] = []
  ): Promise<any> {
    try {
      const response = await axios.post(
        `${WHATSAPP_API_URL}/${this.phoneNumberId}/messages`,
        {
          messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
          to,
          type: 'template',
          template: {
            name: templateName,
            language: { code: language },
            components,
          },
        },
        {
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${this.accessToken}`,
            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          },
        }
      );
      return response.data;
    } catch (error: any) {
      console.error('WhatsApp template error:', error.response?.data || error.message);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  // ─── Mark as Read ────────────────────────────────────────────
  async markAsRead(messageId: string): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await axios.post(
        `${WHATSAPP_API_URL}/${this.phoneNumberId}/messages`,
        {
          messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
          status: 'read',
          message_id: messageId,
        },
        {
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${this.accessToken}`,
            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          },
        }
      );
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Mark as read error:', error);
    }
  }

  // ─── Webhook Verification ────────────────────────────────────
  verifyWebhook(mode: string, token: string, challenge: string): string | null {
    if (mode === 'subscribe' && token === VERIFY_TOKEN) {
      return challenge;
    }
    return null;
  }

  // ─── Handle Incoming Message ────────────────────────────────
  async handleIncomingMessage(body: any): Promise<void> {
    if (body.object !== 'whatsapp_business_account') return;

    for (const entry of body.entry || []) {
      for (const change of entry.changes || []) {
        if (change.field !== 'messages') continue;

        const message = change.value.messages?.[0];
        if (!message) continue;

        const from = message.from;
        const text = message.text?.body;

        // Mark as read
        await this.markAsRead(message.id);

        // Store user phone in DB (if new)
        await this.ensureUser(from);

        // Route to appropriate handler
        if (text) {
          await this.routeMessage(from, text);
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // ─── Route Messages ──────────────────────────────────────────
  private async routeMessage(from: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
    const lower = text.toLowerCase().trim();

    // ── Farmer stock declaration ──
    const stockMatch = lower.match(/stock\s+(\d+)\s*(kg|g|ton)\s+(\w+)/i);
    if (stockMatch) {
      await this.handleStockDeclaration(from, stockMatch);
      return;
    }

    // ── Product search ──
    if (lower.includes('price') || lower.includes('rate') || lower.includes('cost')) {
      await this.handleProductPrice(from, text);
      return;
    }

    // ── Order status ──
    if (lower.includes('order') || lower.includes('track')) {
      await this.handleOrderStatus(from, text);
      return;
    }

    // ── Help / menu ──
    if (lower.includes('help') || lower.includes('menu') || lower.includes('?')) {
      await this.sendHelpMenu(from);
      return;
    }

    // ── Fallback: search product ──
    await this.searchProduct(from, text);
  }

  // ─── Help Menu ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  private async sendHelpMenu(to: string): Promise<void> {
    const menu = `
*NE Harvest — WhatsApp Assistant*
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📦 *Stock declaration:*  
  \`STOCK 50kg honey\`

🔍 *Product price:*  
  \`Price of turmeric\`

📦 *Order tracking:*  
  \`Track order #12345\`

🌿 *Seasonal pre‑order:*  
  \`Pre-order kiwi\`

👨‍🌾 *Farmer support:*  
  \`Scheme PMFME\`

❓ *This menu:*  
  \`Help\`
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reply with a keyword or question.`;
    await this.sendText(to, menu);
  }

  // ─── Stock Declaration ──────────────────────────────────────
  private async handleStockDeclaration(
    from: string,
    match: RegExpMatchArray
  ): Promise<void> {
    const [_, quantity, unit, productName] = match;
    const qty = parseFloat(quantity);

    // Find user by phone
    const user = await prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { phone: from } });
    if (!user) {
      await this.sendText(from, '⚠️ Please register on the platform first.');
      return;
    }

    // Find product
    const product = await prisma.product.findFirst({
      where: { name: { contains: productName, mode: 'insensitive' } },
    });
    if (!product) {
      await this.sendText(from, `❌ Product "${productName}" not found.`);
      return;
    }

    // Create stock declaration
    await prisma.stock.create({
      data: {
        farmerId: user.farmer?.id!,
        productId: product.id,
        quantity: qty,
        unit,
        harvestDate: new Date(),
        status: 'pending',
      },
    });

    await this.sendText(
      from,
      `✅ Stock declared: ${qty}${unit} of ${product.name}.\nStatus: Pending collection.`
    );
  }

  // ─── Product Price ──────────────────────────────────────────
  private async handleProductPrice(from: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
    // Extract product name
    const productName = text.replace(/price|rate|cost|of/gi, '').trim();
    const product = await prisma.product.findFirst({
      where: { name: { contains: productName, mode: 'insensitive' } },
    });
    if (!product) {
      await this.sendText(from, `❌ Product "${productName}" not found.`);
      return;
    }
    await this.sendText(
      from,
      `📊 *${product.name}*\nPrice: ₹${product.price}/${product.unit}\nOrigin: ${product.origin || 'NE India'}\n${product.claim || ''}`
    );
  }

  // ─── Order Status ───────────────────────────────────────────
  private async handleOrderStatus(from: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
    const orderId = text.match(/\d+/)?.[0];
    if (!orderId) {
      await this.sendText(from, 'Please provide an order number.');
      return;
    }
    const order = await prisma.order.findFirst({
      where: { id: parseInt(orderId) },
      include: { user: true },
    });
    if (!order) {
      await this.sendText(from, `❌ Order #${orderId} not found.`);
      return;
    }
    if (order.user.phone !== from) {
      await this.sendText(from, '🔒 This order does not belong to you.');
      return;
    }
    await this.sendText(
      from,
      `📦 *Order #${order.id}*\nStatus: ${order.status}\nTotal: ₹${order.total}\nItems: ${order.items?.length || 0}`
    );
  }

  // ─── Search Product ─────────────────────────────────────────
  private async searchProduct(from: string, query: string): Promise<void> {
    const products = await prisma.product.findMany({
      where: {
        OR: [
          { name: { contains: query, mode: 'insensitive' } },
          { description: { contains: query, mode: 'insensitive' } },
        ],
      },
      take: 5,
    });
    if (products.length === 0) {
      await this.sendText(from, `❌ No products found for "${query}".`);
      return;
    }
    const response =
      '🔍 *Search results:*\n' +
      products.map(p => `• ${p.name} — ₹${p.price}/${p.unit}`).join('\n');
    await this.sendText(from, response);
  }

  // ─── Ensure User by Phone ──────────────────────────────────
  private async ensureUser(phone: string): Promise<void> {
    const existing = await prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { phone } });
    if (!existing) {
      await prisma.user.create({
        data: {
          phone,
          email: `whatsapp_${phone.replace('+', '')}@temp.com`,
          passwordHash: 'whatsapp_placeholder',
          name: `User ${phone.slice(-4)}`,
          role: 'CONSUMER',
        },
      });
    }
  }
}

3.2 WhatsApp Webhook Route — backend/src/routes/whatsapp.ts
typescript
import express from 'express';
import { whatsappClient, VERIFY_TOKEN } from '../services/whatsapp.js';

const router = express.Router();

// ─── Webhook Verification (GET) ──────────────────────────────
router.get('/webhook', (req, res) => {
  const mode = req.query['hub.mode'] as string;
  const token = req.query['hub.verify_token'] as string;
  const challenge = req.query['hub.challenge'] as string;

  const result = whatsappClient.verifyWebhook(mode, token, challenge);
  if (result) {
    res.status(200).send(result);
  } else {
    res.sendStatus(403);
  }
});

// ─── Incoming Messages (POST) ─────────────────────────────────
router.post('/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    await whatsappClient.handleIncomingMessage(req.body);
    res.sendStatus(200);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Webhook error:', error);
    res.sendStatus(500);
  }
});

// ─── Send Notification (Internal) ─────────────────────────────
router.post('/notify', async (req, res) => {
  const { phone, template, params } = req.body;
  try {
    const result = await whatsappClient.sendTemplate(phone, template, 'en', params);
    res.json(result);
  } catch (error) {
    res.status(500).json({ error: (error as Error).message });
  }
});

export default router;
3.3 Notification Service — backend/src/services/notification.ts
typescript
import { whatsappClient } from './whatsapp.js';
import { prisma } from '../server.js';
import { redis } from './redis.js';

type NotificationChannel = 'whatsapp' | 'email' | 'push';

export interface NotificationPayload {
  userId: number;
  channel: NotificationChannel;
  title: string;
  body: string;
  data?: Record<string, any>;
  template?: string;
}

class NotificationService {
  // ─── Send notification (multi‑channel) ──────────────────────
  async send(payload: NotificationPayload): Promise<void> {
    const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
      where: { id: payload.userId },
    });
    if (!user) throw new Error('User not found');

    switch (payload.channel) {
      case 'whatsapp':
        await this.sendWhatsApp(user, payload);
        break;
      case 'email':
        await this.sendEmail(user, payload);
        break;
      case 'push':
        await this.sendPush(user, payload);
        break;
      default:
        console.warn('Unknown channel:', payload.channel);
    }
  }

  // ─── WhatsApp ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  private async sendWhatsApp(user: any, payload: NotificationPayload): Promise<void> {
    if (!user.phone) {
      console.warn(`User ${user.id} has no phone number.`);
      return;
    }

    if (payload.template) {
      await whatsappClient.sendTemplate(user.phone, payload.template, 'en', [
        { type: 'body', parameters: [{ type: 'text', text: payload.body }] },
      ]);
    } else {
      await whatsappClient.sendText(user.phone, `${payload.title}\n${payload.body}`);
    }
  }

  // ─── Email (stub) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  private async sendEmail(user: any, payload: NotificationPayload): Promise<void> {
    // Use Nodemailer, SendGrid, etc.
    console.log(`📧 [Email] to ${user.email}: ${payload.title}`);
  }

  // ─── Push (stub – for mobile app) ───────────────────────────
  private async sendPush(user: any, payload: NotificationPayload): Promise<void> {
    // Use Firebase Cloud Messaging, Expo Notifications, etc.
    console.log(`📱 [Push] to user ${user.id}: ${payload.title}`);
  }

  // ─── Send Order Confirmation ────────────────────────────────
  async sendOrderConfirmation(orderId: number): Promise<void> {
    const order = await prisma.order.findUnique({
      where: { id: orderId },
      include: { user: true, items: { include: { product: true } } },
    });
    if (!order) return;

    const body = `Order #${order.id} confirmed.\nTotal: ₹${order.total}\nItems: ${order.items.length}\nDelivery: Saturday 7–11 AM.`;
    await this.send({
      userId: order.userId,
      channel: 'whatsapp',
      title: '✅ Order Confirmed',
      body,
      template: 'order_confirmation',
      data: { orderId: order.id },
    });
  }

  // ─── Send Daily Nutrition Report ────────────────────────────
  async sendDailyReport(userId: number): Promise<void> {
    // Fetch user’s daily consumption (placeholder)
    const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
    if (!user) return;

    const body = `🌿 Daily Nutrition Report\n• Protein: 65g (120%)\n• Carbs: 210g (85%)\n• Vitamin C: 95mg (106%)\n• Calcium: 850mg (80%)`;
    await this.send({
      userId,
      channel: 'whatsapp',
      title: '📊 Your Daily Nutrition',
      body,
      template: 'daily_nutrition',
    });
  }

  // ─── Farmer Payment Notification ────────────────────────────
  async sendFarmerPayment(farmerId: number, amount: number): Promise<void> {
    const farmer = await prisma.farmer.findUnique({
      where: { id: farmerId },
      include: { user: true },
    });
    if (!farmer) return;

    await this.send({
      userId: farmer.userId,
      channel: 'whatsapp',
      title: '💰 Payment Released',
      body: `₹${amount} has been released to your account.\nTransaction ID: EVD-${Date.now()}`,
      template: 'payment_release',
    });
  }
}

export const notificationService = new NotificationService();

typescript
import express from 'express';
import { notificationService } from '../services/notification.js';
import { authenticate } from '../middleware/auth.js';

const router = express.Router();

// ─── Trigger Daily Report (manual/test) ──────────────────────
router.post('/daily-report', authenticate, async (req, res) => {
  await notificationService.sendDailyReport(req.userId!);
  res.json({ message: 'Daily report sent.' });
});

// ─── Trigger Order Confirmation ───────────────────────────────
router.post('/order-confirmation', authenticate, async (req, res) => {
  const { orderId } = req.body;
  if (!orderId) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'orderId required' });
  await notificationService.sendOrderConfirmation(orderId);
  res.json({ message: 'Order confirmation sent.' });
});

export default router;

import { View, Text, FlatList, TouchableOpacity, Image } from 'react-native';

mobile/store/cartStore.ts
typescript
import { create } from 'zustand';

interface CartItem {
  productId: number;
  name: string;
  price: number;
  unit: string;
  qty: number;
  emoji: string;
}

interface CartState {
  items: CartItem[];
  total: number;
  addItem: (product: any) => void;
  removeItem: (productId: number) => void;
  updateQty: (productId: number, qty: number) => void;
  clear: () => void;
}

export const useCartStore = create<CartState>((set, get) => ({
  items: [],
  total: 0,
  addItem: (product) => {
    set((state) => {
      const existing = state.items.find(i => i.productId === product.id);
      let newItems;
      if (existing) {
        newItems = state.items.map(i =>
          i.productId === product.id ? { ...i, qty: i.qty + 1 } : i
        );
      } else {
        newItems = [...state.items, {
          productId: product.id,
          name: product.name,
          price: product.price,
          unit: product.unit,
          qty: 1,
          emoji: product.emoji,
        }];
      }
      const total = newItems.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty, 0);
      return { items: newItems, total };
    });
  },
  removeItem: (productId) => {
    set((state) => {
      const newItems = state.items.filter(i => i.productId !== productId);
      const total = newItems.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty, 0);
      return { items: newItems, total };
    });
  },
  updateQty: (productId, qty) => {
    set((state) => {
      const newItems = state.items.map(i =>
        i.productId === productId ? { ...i, qty: Math.max(1, qty) } : i
      );
      const total = newItems.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty, 0);
      return { items: newItems, total };
    });
  },
  clear: () => set({ items: [], total: 0 }),
}));
mobile/hooks/useApi.ts

import axios from 'axios';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';

const API_URL = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL || 'http://localhost:5000/api';

export const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: API_URL,
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
});

// Add token interceptor
api.interceptors.request.use(async (config) => {
  const token = await AsyncStorage.getItem('auth_token');
  if (token) {
    config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  }
  return config;
});

// --- Auth helpers ---
export async function login(email: string, password: string) {
  const res = await api.post('/auth/login', { email, password });
  await AsyncStorage.setItem('auth_token', res.data.token);
  return res.data.user;
}

export async function register(data: any) {
  const res = await api.post('/auth/register', data);
  await AsyncStorage.setItem('auth_token', res.data.token);
  return res.data.user;
}

export async function logout() {
  await AsyncStorage.removeItem('auth_token');
}

export async function getCurrentUser() {
  const res = await api.get('/auth/me');
  return res.data;
}

import { app, BrowserWindow, Menu, ipcMain } from 'electron';
import path from 'path';
import { autoUpdater } from 'electron-updater';

let mainWindow: BrowserWindow | null = null;

function createWindow() {
  mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 1200,
    height: 800,
    webPreferences: {
      preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js'),
      nodeIntegration: false,
      contextIsolation: true,
    },
    icon: path.join(__dirname, '../build/icon.png'),
  });

  // Load the Next.js build
  const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development';
  const startUrl = isDev
    ? 'http://localhost:3000'  // dev server
    : `file://${path.join(__dirname, '../../frontend/out/index.html')}`;

  mainWindow.loadURL(startUrl);

  // Auto-updater
  autoUpdater.checkForUpdatesAndNotify();

  mainWindow.on('closed', () => {
    mainWindow = null;
  });
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  createWindow();
  // Build menu
  const template = [
    {
      label: 'File',
      submenu: [
        { role: 'quit' },
      ],
    },
    {
      label: 'View',
      submenu: [
        { role: 'reload' },
        { role: 'forceReload' },
        { role: 'toggleDevTools' },
        { type: 'separator' },
        { role: 'resetZoom' },
        { role: 'zoomIn' },
        { role: 'zoomOut' },
        { type: 'separator' },
        { role: 'togglefullscreen' },
      ],
    },
  ];
  const menu = Menu.buildFromTemplate(template as any);
  Menu.setApplicationMenu(menu);
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => {
  if (process.platform !== 'darwin') app.quit();
});

// ─── Auto-updater ────────────────────────────────────────────
autoUpdater.on('update-available', () => {
  mainWindow?.webContents.send('update-available');
});

autoUpdater.on('update-downloaded', () => {
  mainWindow?.webContents.send('update-downloaded');
});

ipcMain.on('restart-app', () => {
  autoUpdater.quitAndInstall();
});

🏗️ System Architecture Overview

1️⃣ Digital Twin & Metabolic Prediction Engine

# services/digital_twin/prediction_engine.py
import torch
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from app.models.health_models import GlucosePredictionRequest, GlucosePredictionResponse
from app.utils.data_prep import prepare_glucose_sequences
# Hypothetical Gluformer model – you would use a real implementation
from gluformer import GluformerModel  

class MetabolicDigitalTwin:
    """
    Core digital twin engine using a Transformer-based time-series model.
    It maintains per-user state to produce personalised predictions.
    """
    def __init__(self, model_path: str, device: str = "cuda"):
        self.device = torch.device(device if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
        self.model = GluformerModel.from_pretrained(model_path).to(self.device)
        self.model.eval()
        # In-memory cache for recent user data (in production, use Redis)
        self.user_cache: Dict[str, Dict] = {}

    def _get_user_context(self, user_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Retrieve or initialise user context from cache/database."""
        if user_id not in self.user_cache:
            # Load last 24h of glucose, meals, activity from InfluxDB
            self.user_cache[user_id] = self._load_historical_data(user_id)
        return self.user_cache[user_id]

    def _load_historical_data(self, user_id: str, lookback_hours: int = 24):
        """Query InfluxDB for glucose readings, meal logs, and activity."""
        # InfluxDB query – simplified here
        return {
            "glucose": [],   # list of (timestamp, value)
            "meals": [],     # list of (timestamp, carbs, fat, protein)
            "activity": []   # list of (timestamp, steps, heart_rate)
        }

    def predict_glucose(self, user_id: str, request: GlucosePredictionRequest) -> GlucosePredictionResponse:
        """
        Predict future glucose values for the next 30–120 minutes.
        The request includes current glucose, planned meal, and activity.
        """
        context = self._get_user_context(user_id)
        # Build input sequence: last 12 glucose readings (5-min intervals) + features
        X, metadata = self._prepare_features(context, request)
        X_tensor = torch.tensor(X, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)  # batch=1

        with torch.no_grad():
            # Model outputs a sequence of future glucose values (e.g., 24 steps of 5 min)
            pred = self.model(X_tensor)   # shape: (1, pred_len)
            pred_values = pred.squeeze().cpu().numpy().tolist()
            # Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty – run forward passes with dropout enabled
            uncertainties = self._estimate_uncertainty(X_tensor, n_iter=30)

        # Map predictions to timestamps
        start_time = request.current_time or datetime.now()
        timestamps = [start_time + timedelta(minutes=5*i) for i in range(len(pred_values))]

        # Generate an actionable recommendation if hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia is predicted
        action = self._generate_action_plan(pred_values, uncertainties, context)

        return GlucosePredictionResponse(
            user_id=user_id,
            timestamps=timestamps,
            predicted_values=pred_values,
            uncertainty_lower=uncertainties[0],
            uncertainty_upper=uncertainties[1],
            recommended_action=action
        )

    def _prepare_features(self, context: Dict, request: GlucosePredictionRequest) -> tuple:
        """
        Create feature vector: past glucose, meal carbs, activity, time-of-day embeddings.
        """
        # This is a simplified example – real implementation uses more features
        past_glucose = [g['value'] for g in context['glucose'][-12:]]  # last hour at 5-min intervals
        # Pad if less than 12
        if len(past_glucose) < 12:
            past_glucose = [100] * (12 - len(past_glucose)) + past_glucose
        # Add current glucose and meal info from request
        features = past_glucose + [
            request.current_glucose,
            request.planned_carbs or 0,
            request.planned_fat or 0,
            request.planned_protein or 0,
            request.recent_activity or 0
        ]
        # Normalise (assuming pre-trained model expects normalised inputs)
        features = np.array(features) / 200.0  # normalise to ~0-1
        return features, {}

    def _estimate_uncertainty(self, input_tensor, n_iter: int = 30):
        """Use Monte Carlo Dropout to estimate prediction intervals."""
        self.model.train()  # enable dropout
        preds = []
        for _ in range(n_iter):
            with torch.no_grad():
                pred = self.model(input_tensor)
                preds.append(pred.squeeze().cpu().numpy())
        self.model.eval()
        preds = np.array(preds)
        lower = np.percentile(preds, 5, axis=0)
        upper = np.percentile(preds, 95, axis=0)
        return lower.tolist(), upper.tolist()

    def _generate_action_plan(self, predictions, uncertainties, context):
        """If hypoglycemia (<70) or hyperglycemia (>180) predicted, suggest corrective action."""
        min_pred = min(predictions)
        max_pred = max(predictions)
        if min_pred < 70:
            return {"alert": "hypoglycemia_risk", "suggestion": "Consume 15g fast-acting carbs and re-check in 15 min."}
        elif max_pred > 180:
            return {"alert": "hyperglycemia_risk", "suggestion": "Take a 15-min walk or adjust insulin dosage (consult physician)."}
        return {"alert": "stable", "suggestion": "Your glucose is expected to remain in range."}

    def simulate_meal_impact(self, user_id: str, meal_data: dict) -> dict:
        """
        What‑if analysis: simulate the effect of a hypothetical meal on future glucose.
        """
        # Create a copy of user context, override meal parameters, run prediction
        request = GlucosePredictionRequest(
            current_glucose=self.user_cache[user_id]['glucose'][-1]['value'],
            planned_carbs=meal_data.get('carbs', 0),
            planned_fat=meal_data.get('fat', 0),
            planned_protein=meal_data.get('protein', 0),
            current_time=datetime.now()
        )
        # Run prediction with these parameters
        result = self.predict_glucose(user_id, request)
        return {
            "simulated_curve": result.predicted_values,
            "peak_glucose": max(result.predicted_values),
            "time_to_peak": result.timestamps[np.argmax(result.predicted_values)].isoformat()
        }

# services/nutrigenomics/dna_analyzer.py
import pandas as pd
import io
from typing import List, Dict
from genebe import GeneBeClient  # Hypothetical client for variant annotation
from app.models.health_models import GeneticReport

class NutrigenomicsService:
    """
    Process raw genetic data to produce actionable nutritional insights.
    """
    def __init__(self, api_key: str):
        self.gb_client = GeneBeClient(api_key=api_key)
        # Load a curated SNP database with nutritional relevance
        self.snp_db = pd.read_csv("data/nutritional_snps.csv")
        # e.g., columns: rsid, gene, risk_allele, effect, recommendation

    def analyze_raw_dna(self, file_content: bytes, file_format: str = "23andme") -> GeneticReport:
        """
        Parse and analyse a raw DNA file.
        Returns a report with genotype-specific dietary advice.
        """
        # 1. Parse file
        if file_format == "23andme":
            # 23andMe format: header lines start with '#', then columns: rsid, chromosome, position, genotype
            df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(file_content.decode('utf-8')), comment='#', header=None,
                             names=['rsid', 'chromosome', 'position', 'genotype'])
        elif file_format == "vcf":
            # Use pysam or vcfpy to parse VCF – simplified here
            raise NotImplementedError("VCF parsing not implemented")
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported file format")

        # 2. Filter for known nutrition SNPs
        relevant = df[df['rsid'].isin(self.snp_db['rsid'])]
        if relevant.empty:
            return GeneticReport(insights=[], message="No known nutrition SNPs found.")

        # 3. Annotate with GeneBe (or other) to get gene names, consequences
        variants = relevant[['rsid', 'genotype']].to_dict('records')
        annotated = self.gb_client.annotate_variants(variants)

        # 4. Generate recommendations
        recommendations = []
        for ann in annotated:
            rsid = ann['rsid']
            gene = ann.get('gene', 'unknown')
            user_genotype = ann['user_genotype']  # e.g., 'AA', 'AG', 'GG'
            # Find matching entry in our SNP DB
            row = self.snp_db[self.snp_db['rsid'] == rsid]
            if not row.empty:
                row = row.iloc[0]
                risk_allele = row['risk_allele']
                # If user carries risk allele (heterozygous or homozygous)
                if risk_allele in user_genotype:
                    advice = row['recommendation']
                    recommendations.append({
                        "gene": gene,
                        "variant": rsid,
                        "genotype": user_genotype,
                        "recommendation": advice,
                        "evidence": row.get('evidence', '')
                    })
                else:
                    # beneficial genotype – maybe note "no action required"
                    pass
        return GeneticReport(insights=recommendations, message="Analysis complete.")

    def integrate_with_microbiome(self, user_id: str, dna_report: GeneticReport, microbiome_data: dict):
        """
        Combine genetic and microbiome insights for a unified precision nutrition plan.
        """

python
# services/cgm/cgm_service.py
from pydexcom import Dexcom
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import json
from app.models.health_models import CGMReading
from app.utils.influx_client import InfluxWriter
from app.events import publish_event

class CGMService:
    """
    Manages Dexcom session, fetches readings, and processes webhook notifications.
    """
    def __init__(self, username: str, password: str, region: str = "us", influx_url: str = None):
        self.dexcom = Dexcom(username=username, password=password, region=region)
        self.influx = InfluxWriter(url=influx_url, org="health", bucket="cgm")
        # For webhook authentication, we store a secret per user
        self.webhook_secrets = {}  # In production, use database

    def get_latest_reading(self, user_id: str) -> CGMReading:
        """
        Get the most recent glucose value from Dexcom.
        """
        reading = self.dexcom.get_current_glucose_reading()
        return CGMReading(
            user_id=user_id,
            value=reading.value,
            unit="mg/dL",
            trend=reading.trend_description,
            timestamp=reading.datetime,
            device="dexcom"
        )

    def get_historical_readings(self, user_id: str, start: datetime, end: datetime) -> List[CGMReading]:
        """
        Retrieve a range of historical readings for model training or visualisation.
        """
        readings = self.dexcom.get_glucose_readings(start, end)
        return [CGMReading(user_id=user_id, value=r.value, timestamp=r.datetime, device="dexcom")
                for r in readings]

    def process_webhook(self, payload: dict, signature: str) -> dict:
        """
        Handle incoming webhook from Dexcom (or other provider).
        Validate signature, parse the data, store in InfluxDB, and trigger analysis.
        """
        # Verify signature (assuming HMAC-SHA256)
        user_id = payload.get('user_id')
        secret = self.webhook_secrets.get(user_id)
        if not secret:
            raise ValueError("Unknown user or missing secret")
        # Validate signature – simplified
        # if not self._validate_signature(payload, signature, secret): raise ...

        # Extract reading(s)
        readings = payload.get('readings', [])
        for r in readings:
            reading = CGMReading(
                user_id=user_id,
                value=r['value'],
                unit=r['unit'],
                trend=r.get('trend'),
                timestamp=datetime.fromisoformat(r['timestamp']),
                device=r.get('device', 'dexcom')
            )
            # Write to InfluxDB
            self.influx.write_reading(reading)
            # Publish event for downstream services (digital twin, alerts)
            publish_event('cgm.new_reading', reading.dict())

        return {"status": "processed", "count": len(readings)}

    def _validate_signature(self, payload, signature, secret):
        # Implement signature validation as per Dexcom's webhook spec
        return True
4️⃣ Agentic AI Orchestrator (LangGraph)
This is the brain of the autonomous coaching system. It routes user queries to specialised agents, each equipped with tools.

python
# agents/health_coach_orchestrator.py
from typing import Literal
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from app.agents.dietitian_agent import dietitian_node
from app.agents.fitness_agent import fitness_node
from app.agents.therapist_agent import therapist_node
from app.agents.tools import search_web, get_meal_plan, log_water, fetch_wearable_data

class HealthCoachOrchestrator:
    """
    Multi-agent system using LangGraph.
    Supervisor decides which specialist agent to invoke based on user intent.
    """
    def __init__(self, llm_model: str = "gpt-4o"):
        self.llm = ChatOpenAI(model=llm_model, temperature=0)
        # Define the graph
        self.workflow = StateGraph(dict)

        # Add nodes: supervisor and specialist agents
        self.workflow.add_node("supervisor", self.supervisor_node)
        self.workflow.add_node("dietitian", dietitian_node)   # can call tools
        self.workflow.add_node("fitness", fitness_node)
        self.workflow.add_node("therapist", therapist_node)

        # Define edges
        self.workflow.add_conditional_edges(
            "supervisor",
            self.route_decision,
            {
                "dietitian": "dietitian",
                "fitness": "fitness",
                "therapist": "therapist",
                "FINISH": END
            }
        )
        # After specialist, always go back to supervisor (or end)
        self.workflow.add_edge("dietitian", "supervisor")
        self.workflow.add_edge("fitness", "supervisor")
        self.workflow.add_edge("therapist", "supervisor")

        # Set entry point
        self.workflow.set_entry_point("supervisor")
        self.app = self.workflow.compile()

    def supervisor_node(self, state: dict) -> dict:
        """
        Supervisor: decides which agent to call next based on the conversation history.
        """
        messages = state.get("messages", [])
        # Prepare prompt for the supervisor
        sys_msg = SystemMessage(content="""You are the chief health orchestrator. 
        Determine which specialist is best suited to handle the user's current request.
        Available specialists: 'dietitian' (nutrition, meal plans), 'fitness' (exercise, activity), 
        'therapist' (emotional support, behaviour change).
        If the request is resolved, respond with 'FINISH'.
        Output only one of: dietitian, fitness, therapist, FINISH.
        """)
        # We can include a special instruction to force a decision
        response = self.llm.invoke([sys_msg] + messages)
        next_step = response.content.strip().lower()
        # Ensure it's a valid option
        if next_step not in ["dietitian", "fitness", "therapist", "finish"]:
            next_step = "finish"  # fallback
        state["next_step"] = next_step
        return state

    def route_decision(self, state: dict) -> Literal["dietitian", "fitness", "therapist", "FINISH"]:
        step = state.get("next_step", "finish").upper()
        if step == "FINISH":
            return "FINISH"
        return step

    def process_request(self, user_id: str, query: str) -> dict:
        """
        Entry point for a user request.
        """
        initial_state = {
            "messages": [HumanMessage(content=query)],
            "user_id": user_id,
            "next_step": "supervisor"
        }
        final_state = self.app.invoke(initial_state)
        return {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "response": final_state.get("messages", [])[-1].content,
            "full_trace": final_state
        }
Example Dietitian Agent (with tools):

# agents/dietitian_agent.py
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode

@tool
def get_meal_plan(user_id: str, date: str) -> str:
    """Retrieve the pre-generated meal plan for a user on a given date."""
    # Call internal API or database
    return "Breakfast: oatmeal, Lunch: salad, Dinner: fish"

@tool
def log_food(user_id: str, food: str, calories: int) -> str:
    """Log a food entry for the user."""
    # Save to database
    return f"Logged {food} ({calories} cal) for user {user_id}"

tools = [get_meal_plan, log_food]
tool_node = ToolNode(tools)

def dietitian_node(state: dict) -> dict:
    """
    Dietitian agent: uses tools to answer nutrition-related queries.
    """
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0.3).bind_tools(tools)
    messages = state.get("messages", [])
    # Add a system prompt
    sys_msg = SystemMessage(content="You are a clinical dietitian. Use the provided tools to assist the user.")
    response = llm.invoke([sys_msg] + messages)
    # If tool calls are requested, the next step would invoke tool_node – but for simplicity we just return the message
    state["messages"].append(AIMessage(content=response.content))
    return state
5️⃣ Explainable AI (XAI) Recommendation Engine
This service provides interpretable food recommendations using SHAP.

python
# services/recommendation/xai_explainer.py
import shap
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor
from typing import List, Dict

class ExplainableFoodRecommender:
    """
    Recommends foods based on a trained model and explains why each is chosen.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        # In production, load a pre-trained model from disk
        self.model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
        # Assume we have a feature matrix X_train and target y_train
        # self.model.fit(X_train, y_train)
        # For SHAP, we need a background dataset (sample of training data)
        self.background = None  # Load from file
        self.explainer = shap.KernelExplainer(self.model.predict, self.background)

        # Feature names for interpretation
        self.feature_names = [
            'user_age', 'user_bmi', 'user_goal', 'user_taste_pref',
            'food_calories', 'food_protein', 'food_carbs', 'food_fat',
            'food_fiber', 'food_sugar', 'food_sodium'
        ]

    def recommend(self, user_id: str, candidate_foods: List[Dict]) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        For a list of candidate food items, compute a predicted score (e.g., healthiness fit)
        and explain the top recommendations.
        """
        # Generate feature vectors for each candidate (user features + food features)
        user_features = self._get_user_features(user_id)
        X = []
        for food in candidate_foods:
            features = user_features + [
                food.get('calories', 0),
                food.get('protein', 0),
                food.get('carbs', 0),
                food.get('fat', 0),
                food.get('fiber', 0),
                food.get('sugar', 0),
                food.get('sodium', 0)
            ]
            X.append(features)
        X = np.array(X)
        # Predict scores
        scores = self.model.predict(X)
        # Compute SHAP values for the entire batch
        shap_values = self.explainer.shap_values(X)

        # Build recommendation list with explanations
        recommendations = []
        for i, food in enumerate(candidate_foods):
            # Get top 3 features contributing to this prediction (SHAP)
            shap_contrib = shap_values[i]
            # Find indices of highest absolute SHAP values
            top_idx = np.argsort(np.abs(shap_contrib))[-3:][::-1]
            top_features = [(self.feature_names[j], shap_contrib[j]) for j in top_idx]

            explanation = {
                "summary": f"Predicted score: {scores[i]:.2f}. "
                           f"This recommendation is mainly driven by {', '.join([f[0] for f in top_features])}.",
                "details": top_features
            }
            recommendations.append({
                "food": food,
                "score": scores[i],
                "explanation": explanation
            })
        # Sort by descending score
        recommendations.sort(key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)
        return recommendations

    def _get_user_features(self, user_id: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieve user profile features from database."""
        # Placeholder – return dummy values
        return [34.0, 24.5, 1.0, 0.5]  # age, bmi, goal, taste_pref
6️⃣ Chrono‑Nutrition (Meal Timing Optimisation)
This service computes optimal eating windows based on the user's sunrise/sunset and sleep patterns.

python
# services/chrono/meal_timing_optimizer.py
import requests
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict

class ChronoNutritionOptimizer:
    """
    Uses sunrise/sunset data and user sleep schedule to recommend meal times.
    """
    SUNRISE_SUNSET_API = "https://api.sunrise-sunset.org/json"

    def get_sun_times(self, lat: float, lng: float, date: str) -> Dict:
        """Fetch sunrise and sunset times for a given location and date."""
        params = {
            "lat": lat,
            "lng": lng,
            "date": date,
            "formatted": 0  # return ISO 8601
        }
        response = requests.get(self.SUNRISE_SUNSET_API, params=params)
        response.raise_for_status()
        data = response.json()['results']
        return {
            "sunrise": datetime.fromisoformat(data['sunrise']),
            "sunset": datetime.fromisoformat(data['sunset'])
        }

    def optimize_meal_times(self, user_id: str, date: str) -> Dict[str, datetime]:
        """
        Compute recommended meal windows based on circadian biology.
        """
        # Get user's location and typical sleep times from database
        user = self._get_user_profile(user_id)
        sun = self.get_sun_times(user.lat, user.lng, date)
        # Assume user wakes up ~30 min after sunrise and sleeps ~4h after sunset (adjustable)
        wake_time = sun['sunrise'] + timedelta(minutes=30)
        sleep_time = sun['sunset'] + timedelta(hours=4)

        # Define meal windows (based on chrono-nutrition research)
        # Breakfast: within 1-2 hours of waking
        breakfast_start = wake_time + timedelta(hours=1)
        breakfast_end = wake_time + timedelta(hours=2)
        # Lunch: 4-5 hours after waking
        lunch_start = wake_time + timedelta(hours=4.5)
        lunch_end = wake_time + timedelta(hours=5.5)
        # Dinner: 9-10 hours after waking (at least 3h before sleep)
        dinner_start = wake_time + timedelta(hours=9)
        dinner_end = wake_time + timedelta(hours=10)

        return {
            "breakfast": {"start": breakfast_start, "end": breakfast_end},
            "lunch": {"start": lunch_start, "end": lunch_end},
            "dinner": {"start": dinner_start, "end": dinner_end}
        }

    def _get_user_profile(self, user_id: str):
        """Fetch user profile from DB."""
        # Placeholder
        return type('User', (), {'lat': 40.7128, 'lng': -74.0060})()
7️⃣ Voice Interaction Service
This service uses Groq's Whisper API for fast, accurate speech‑to‑text.

python
# services/voice/voice_service.py
import base64
from groq import Groq
from fastapi import UploadFile, File
from app.services.nlu import NLUService  # hypothetical NLU for intent parsing

class VoiceInteractionService:
    def __init__(self, api_key: str):
        self.groq = Groq(api_key=api_key)
        self.nlu = NLUService()

    async def transcribe_audio(self, audio_file: UploadFile) -> str:
        """
        Convert audio (WAV/MP3) to text using Groq's Whisper model.
        """
        # Read file contents
        audio_bytes = await audio_file.read()
        # Groq expects a file-like object; we can create a temporary file or use BytesIO
        import io
        audio_io = io.BytesIO(audio_bytes)
        audio_io.name = audio_file.filename  # Groq uses filename to infer format

        transcription = self.groq.audio.transcriptions.create(
            file=audio_io,
            model="whisper-large-v3-turbo",
            response_format="text",
            language="en"
        )
        return transcription

    async def process_voice_command(self, audio_file: UploadFile, user_id: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Full pipeline: transcribe, parse intent, execute action.
        """
        text = await self.transcribe_audio(audio_file)
        intent = self.nlu.parse_intent(text)
        # Execute the intent (e.g., log meal, ask for plan, etc.)
        result = await self.execute_intent(user_id, intent, text)
        return {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "transcript": text,
            "intent": intent,
            "result": result
        }

    async def execute_intent(self, user_id: str, intent: dict, original_text: str):
        """
        Route to appropriate handler based on intent.
        """
        intent_type = intent.get('type')
        if intent_type == 'log_food':
            # Extract food and calories from intent
            food = intent.get('food')
            calories = intent.get('calories')
            # Call logging service
            return {"status": "logged", "food": food, "calories": calories}
        elif intent_type == 'get_plan':
            # Return today's meal plan
            return {"plan": "Your meals for today: ..."}
        else:
            return {"message": "I didn't understand that command."}

Here is a deep dive into both Gluformer’s model architecture and LangGraph’s tool implementation, with detailed code and architectural explanations.

🧬 PART 1: Gluformer – Transformer-Based Glucose Forecasting with Uncertainty Quantification
1.1 Core Problem It Solves
Traditional glucose forecasting models minimize Mean Squared Error (MSE), which implicitly assumes homogeneous Gaussian noise. This assumption fails in practice because glucose trajectories are:

Highly non-linear and non-stationary

Multi-modal and skewed

Often have heterogeneous variance across different glucose ranges

The clinical risk: A predicted glucose increase might prompt a patient to take insulin, but if the prediction is wrong, it could lead to dangerous hypoglycemia. Therefore, uncertainty quantification is essential for clinical adoption.

1.2 Key Innovation: Infinite Mixture Model (IMM)
Instead of predicting a single point value, Gluformer models the future glucose trajectory as an infinite mixture of basis distributions (Gaussian, Laplace, etc.). This allows it to:

Capture multi-modal and skewed distributions

Learn uncertainty directly from data

Produce more accurate predictions when trajectories are heterogeneous

Since an IMM has infinite parameters, the authors introduce an approximation: they inject randomness into the network’s computations and treat each output as a realization from one of the mixture components.

1.3 Architecture Overview
Gluformer uses a Transformer encoder-decoder architecture:

text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         GLUFORMER ARCHITECTURE                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                     ENCODER (Transformer)                          │   │
│   │   Input: Past glucose values + subject ID + timestamps             │   │
│   │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│   │   │   Positional Encoding → Multi-Head Self-Attention → FFN    │  │   │
│   │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                    │                                        │
│                                    ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                     DECODER (Transformer)                          │   │
│   │   Output: Parameters of the predictive distribution                │   │
│   │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│   │   │   Masked Self-Attention → Cross-Attention → FFN            │  │   │
│   │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                    │                                        │
│                                    ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │              INFINITE MIXTURE MODEL (IMM) Layer                    │   │
│   │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│   │   │   Output: μ₁, σ₁, π₁, μ₂, σ₂, π₂, ... for each time step  │  │   │
│   │   │   (mean, variance, weight for each mixture component)      │  │   │
│   │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                    │                                        │
│                                    ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │              PREDICTED DISTRIBUTIONS (per time step)               │   │
│   │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│   │   │   p(yₜ) = Σᵢ πᵢ · 𝒩(yₜ | μᵢ, σᵢ²)                       │  │   │
│   │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Step 2: Load Pre-trained Model from Hugging Face
python
# services/digital_twin/gluformer_model.py
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoConfig
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import torch
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional

class GluformerPredictor:
    """
    Wrapper for the Gluformer model from Hugging Face.
    Provides glucose forecasting with uncertainty quantification.
    """
    def __init__(self, model_name: str = "njeffrie/Gluformer"):
        """
        Initialize the Gluformer model.
        Model card: https://huggingface.co/njeffrie/Gluformer
        """
        self.config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
            model_name, 
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
            model_name,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        self.model.eval()
        
        # Model parameters from config
        self.sequence_length = self.config.len_seq  # number of past glucose readings
        self.prediction_horizon = self.config.pred_len  # number of future readings
        self.interval_minutes = 5  # 5-minute intervals[reference:20]
        
    def predict(
        self, 
        subject_id: int,
        past_glucose: List[float],
        timestamps: List[datetime]
    ) -> Tuple[List[float], List[float]]:
        """
        Predict future glucose values with uncertainty.
        
        Args:
            subject_id: Unique identifier for the user
            past_glucose: List of past glucose readings (mg/dL)
            timestamps: Corresponding timestamps (5-min intervals)
            
        Returns:
            predictions: List of predicted glucose values (5-min increments)
            log_variances: List of log variances (uncertainty measure)[reference:21]
        """
        # Validate input length
        if len(past_glucose) != self.sequence_length:
            # Pad or truncate to match expected sequence length
            past_glucose = self._adjust_sequence_length(past_glucose)
            timestamps = self._adjust_timestamps(timestamps)
        
        # Model expects: (subject_id, timestamps, input_glucose)
        with torch.no_grad():
            pred, log_var = self.model(
                subject_id, 
                timestamps, 
                past_glucose
            )
        
        # pred: future glucose values in 5-minute increments[reference:22]
        # log_var: log variance indicating confidence[reference:23]
        return pred.tolist(), log_var.tolist()
    
    def predict_with_confidence_interval(
        self,
        subject_id: int,
        past_glucose: List[float],
        timestamps: List[datetime],
        confidence_level: float = 0.95
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Predict glucose with confidence intervals.
        
        Returns:
            {
                "predictions": [120, 125, 130, ...],
                "lower_bound": [115, 118, 122, ...],
                "upper_bound": [125, 132, 138, ...],
                "timestamps": [...]
            }
        """
        pred, log_var = self.predict(subject_id, past_glucose, timestamps)
        
        # Convert log variance to standard deviation
        variances = np.exp(log_var)
        std_devs = np.sqrt(variances)
        
        # Z-score for confidence level (e.g., 1.96 for 95%)
        from scipy.stats import norm
        z_score = norm.ppf((1 + confidence_level) / 2)
        
        lower_bound = [p - z_score * s for p, s in zip(pred, std_devs)]
        upper_bound = [p + z_score * s for p, s in zip(pred, std_devs)]
        
        # Generate timestamps for predictions
        last_time = timestamps[-1]
        future_timestamps = [
            last_time + timedelta(minutes=self.interval_minutes * (i + 1))
            for i in range(len(pred))
        ]
        
        return {
            "predictions": pred,
            "lower_bound": lower_bound,
            "upper_bound": upper_bound,
            "timestamps": [t.isoformat() for t in future_timestamps],
            "confidence_level": confidence_level
        }
    
    def _adjust_sequence_length(self, glucose: List[float]) -> List[float]:
        """Pad or truncate glucose sequence to match model expectations."""
        if len(glucose) > self.sequence_length:
            return glucose[-self.sequence_length:]
        elif len(glucose) < self.sequence_length:
            # Pad with last value (or use a default)
            pad_value = glucose[-1] if glucose else 100.0
            return [pad_value] * (self.sequence_length - len(glucose)) + glucose
        return glucose
    
    def _adjust_timestamps(self, timestamps: List[datetime]) -> List[datetime]:
        """Ensure timestamps are at 5-minute intervals."""
        if len(timestamps) > self.sequence_length:
            return timestamps[-self.sequence_length:]
        elif len(timestamps) < self.sequence_length:
            # Generate synthetic timestamps
            last_ts = timestamps[-1] if timestamps else datetime.now()
            return [
                last_ts - timedelta(minutes=5 * (self.sequence_length - i))
                for i in range(self.sequence_length - len(timestamps), 0, -1)
            ] + timestamps
        return timestamps
Step 3: Training on Custom Data

# services/digital_twin/train_gluformer.py
"""
Training Gluformer on custom CGM data.
Based on the official repository structure[reference:24]
"""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from gluformer.model import GluformerModel  # From official repo
from gludata.data_loader import GlucoseDataset  # From official repo
import numpy as np

class GluformerTrainer:
    def __init__(
        self,
        model_config: dict,
        learning_rate: float = 1e-4,
        batch_size: int = 64,
        epochs: int = 100
    ):
        self.model = GluformerModel(**model_config)
        self.optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.epochs = epochs
        
    def train(self, train_data_path: str, val_data_path: str):
        """
        Train the Gluformer model on CGM data.
        The official repository uses PyTorch Dataset[reference:25]
        """
        # Load datasets using official data loader[reference:26]
        train_dataset = GlucoseDataset(train_data_path)
        val_dataset = GlucoseDataset(val_data_path)
        
        train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=self.batch_size, shuffle=True)
        val_loader = DataLoader(val_dataset, batch_size=self.batch_size)
        
        # Negative log-likelihood loss for IMM
        # The model outputs distribution parameters, not point estimates
        criterion = nn.NLLLoss()  # Simplified; actual loss is more complex
        
        for epoch in range(self.epochs):
            self.model.train()
            train_loss = 0.0
            
            for batch in train_loader:
                # batch contains: past_glucose, future_glucose, subject_ids, timestamps
                past_glucose, future_glucose, subject_ids, timestamps = batch
                
                self.optimizer.zero_grad()
                
                # Forward pass: predict distribution parameters
                # The model outputs mixture parameters for each future time step
                pred_params = self.model(subject_ids, timestamps, past_glucose)
                
                # Compute negative log-likelihood loss
                # This is where the IMM loss is calculated[reference:27]
                loss = self._compute_imm_loss(pred_params, future_glucose)
                
                loss.backward()
                self.optimizer.step()
                train_loss += loss.item()
            
            # Validation
            self.model.eval()
            val_loss = 0.0
            with torch.no_grad():
                for batch in val_loader:
                    # ... similar to training
                    pass
            
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{self.epochs}, Train Loss: {train_loss:.4f}, Val Loss: {val_loss:.4f}")
    
    def _compute_imm_loss(self, pred_params, targets):
        """
        Compute the Infinite Mixture Model loss.
        The paper describes injecting randomness into network outputs
        and treating each as a realization from a mixture component[reference:28]
        """
        # pred_params contains: [means, variances, mixture_weights] for each time step
        # This is a simplified implementation

Step 4: Integration into Digital Twin Service
python
# services/digital_twin/prediction_engine.py (extended)
from app.services.digital_twin.gluformer_model import GluformerPredictor
from app.services.cgm.cgm_service import CGMService
from app.models.health_models import GlucosePredictionRequest, GlucosePredictionResponse

class MetabolicDigitalTwin:
    def __init__(self, model_path: str = "njeffrie/Gluformer"):
        self.gluformer = GluformerPredictor(model_name=model_path)
        self.cgm_service = CGMService(username="...", password="...")
        # Cache for user contexts
        self.user_cache = {}
    
    def predict_glucose(self, user_id: str, request: GlucosePredictionRequest):
        """
        Predict future glucose using Gluformer with uncertainty quantification.
        """
        # Get user's CGM history (last N readings at 5-min intervals)
        cgm_data = self.cgm_service.get_historical_readings(
            user_id,
            start=datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=2),  # Last 2 hours
            end=datetime.now()
        )
        
        # Extract glucose values and timestamps
        past_glucose = [r.value for r in cgm_data]
        timestamps = [r.timestamp for r in cgm_data]
        
        # Get subject_id (mapped from user_id)
        subject_id = self._get_subject_id(user_id)
        
        # Run Gluformer prediction
        result = self.gluformer.predict_with_confidence_interval(
            subject_id=subject_id,
            past_glucose=past_glucose,
            timestamps=timestamps,
            confidence_level=0.95
        )
        
        # Generate action recommendations based on predictions
        action = self._generate_action_plan(
            result["predictions"],
            result["lower_bound"],
            result["upper_bound"]
        )
        
        return GlucosePredictionResponse(
            user_id=user_id,
            timestamps=[datetime.fromisoformat(t) for t in result["timestamps"]],
            predicted_values=result["predictions"],
            uncertainty_lower=result["lower_bound"],
            uncertainty_upper=result["upper_bound"],
            recommended_action=action
        )

🛠️ PART 2: LangGraph Tool Implementation – Deep Dive
LangGraph provides a flexible framework for building agentic systems. The ToolNode is a prebuilt component that automatically executes tool calls.

2.1 Core Concepts
Concept	Description
Tool	A function that an agent can call to perform an action (decorated with @tool)
ToolNode	Prebuilt node that executes tool calls automatically
tools_condition	Helper that routes to ToolNode when LLM requests a tool call
bind_tools	Method to attach tools to an LLM so it knows they exist
2.2 Complete Tool Implementation
python
# agents/tools/health_tools.py
"""
Comprehensive set of tools for the health coach agent.
Each tool is decorated with @tool and includes:
- A descriptive name (function name)
- A docstring (used by the LLM to understand when to call it)
- Type hints for parameter validation
"""
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from typing import Optional, List, Dict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import json

# ============= Nutrition Tools =============

@tool
def get_meal_plan(user_id: str, date: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Retrieve the pre-generated meal plan for a user on a specific date.
    
    Args:
        user_id: The unique identifier for the user
        date: The date in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)
    
    Returns:
        A string containing the meal plan with breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks
    """
    if date is None:
        date = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    
    # In production: query database
    # For demo: return mock data
    return f"""
    Meal Plan for {date}:
    Breakfast: Oatmeal with berries and almonds (350 cal)
    Lunch: Grilled chicken salad with avocado (480 cal)
    Dinner: Salmon with quinoa and roasted vegetables (620 cal)
    Snacks: Apple (95 cal), Greek yogurt (120 cal)
    Total: 1,665 calories
    """

@tool
def log_food(
    user_id: str, 
    food_name: str, 
    calories: int,
    meal_type: str = "snack",
    protein_g: Optional[float] = None,
    carbs_g: Optional[float] = None,
    fat_g: Optional[float] = None
) -> str:
    """
    Log a food entry for a user.
    
    Args:
        user_id: The user's unique identifier
        food_name: Name of the food item
        calories: Calorie count
        meal_type: breakfast, lunch, dinner, or snack
        protein_g: Protein in grams (optional)
        carbs_g: Carbohydrates in grams (optional)
        fat_g: Fat in grams (optional)
    
    Returns:
        Confirmation message with the logged entry
    """
    # In production: insert into database
    # For demo: return confirmation
    return f"Logged '{food_name}' ({calories} cal) as {meal_type} for user {user_id}"

@tool
def search_food_nutrition(food_name: str) -> str:
    """
    Search for nutritional information about a food item.
    Uses Nutritionix or USDA API.
    
    Args:
        food_name: Name of the food to search for
    
    Returns:
        Nutritional information including calories, macros, and serving size
    """
    # In production: call Nutritionix API
    # For demo: return mock data
    nutrition_data = {
        "apple": {"calories": 95, "protein": 0.5, "carbs": 25, "fat": 0.3},
        "chicken breast": {"calories": 165, "protein": 31, "carbs": 0, "fat": 3.6},
        "salmon": {"calories": 208, "protein": 22, "carbs": 0, "fat": 13},
    }
    
    food_lower = food_name.lower()
    if food_lower in nutrition_data:
        data = nutrition_data[food_lower]
        return f"{food_name}: {data['calories']} cal, Protein: {data['protein']}g, Carbs: {data['carbs']}g, Fat: {data['fat']}g"
    else:
        return f"No nutritional data found for '{food_name}'"
